Define $q^*B$ levelwise by $q_p^{-1}B$, and define $q_*F$ as the equalizer of the two face maps $q_{0*}F_0\rightrightarrows q_{1*}F_1$. A map into this equalizer gives compatible maps at every level by the vertex projections: the equalizer condition makes all vertex choices agree, and the simplicial identities give compatibility with every operator. The inverse/direct-image adjunction therefore gives $q^*\dashv q_*$; $q^*$ is exact.

**Coinduction and levelwise injectivity.** Set $(N_pI)_m=\prod_{\alpha:[m]\to[p]}(Z_\alpha)_*I$, with structure maps induced by composition. The identity component gives $\operatorname{Hom}(F,N_pI)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_p,I)$; hence $N_pI$ is injective for injective $I$. Functorial embeddings $F_p\hookrightarrow I_p$ give $F\hookrightarrow\prod_pN_pI_p$, detected by the identity component at each level. AC and [F4] make this product injective. Each level of $N_pI$ is a finite product of direct images of injectives, hence injective by [F2], [F4]; the same holds for each level of $\prod_pN_pI_p$. Any injective simplicial sheaf is a retract of its such embedding and is consequently injective at each level. Iteration on cokernels resolves sheaves; the bounded-below replacement construction of [F3], using these explicit embeddings at its successive stages, resolves complexes without changing a supplied lower bound.

Its degree-$m$ augmentation cochains are $A^{\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta([m],[p])}$, with the alternating face differential. The augmentation $A\to A^{p+1}$ sends $a$ to the constant tuple. On cochains define $(hc)(i_0,\ldots,i_{m-1})=c(0,i_0,\ldots,i_{m-1})$ and in degree zero evaluate at vertex $0$. Deleting the inserted vertex gives the identity and all other deletions cancel in pairs, so $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}$ on the augmented complex. Products of these contractions and their restrictions to retracts give an exact augmented complex $0\to q_*J\to q_{0*}J_0\to q_{1*}J_1\to\cdots$ for every injective simplicial sheaf $J$. **Ordinary Cartesian descent.** Cartesian means that every structure map is an isomorphism. For a Cartesian sheaf $F$ and a local section $s_i:V_i\to P$, put $B_i=s_i^{-1}F_0$. The two face maps to $F_1$ identify the pullbacks of $F_0$ along the two projections. Pulling this identification back by $z\mapsto(s_i(q(z)),z)$ gives $q^{-1}B_i\simeq F_0$ over $q^{-1}V_i$; vertex projections then give $q_p^{-1}B_i\simeq F_p$. On overlaps, pull the same identification back by $(s_i,s_j):V_i\cap V_j\to P\times_S P$. The degree-two identities give the cocycle equation on triple overlaps, and the diagonal degeneracy gives the identity equation. The sheaf axiom glues the $B_i$ to $B$ on $S$ and their identifications to $q^*B\simeq F$. The same construction glues morphisms, so it is an equivalence of ordinary sheaf categories onto Cartesian sheaves.

set. A function $f:U\to A$ on an open subset $U\subseteq X$ is **locally
constant** when every $x\in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ with
$x\in V$ on which $f$ is constant. Let $A_{\mathrm{pt}}$ be the **constant
presheaf** with value $A$, $A_{\mathrm{pt}}(U)=A$ for every open $U$ with all
restriction maps the identity ([[def-presheaf-on-topological-space]]), and let
$$A_X:=aA_{\mathrm{pt}}$$
be its sheafification ([[def-sheafification]]), the **constant sheaf** with
value $A$ on $X$. Then:

1. the assignment $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}(U):=\{f:U\to A\text{ locally
   constant}\}$, with the usual restriction maps, is a sheaf of sets on $X$, and
   for every $x\in X$ evaluation at $x$ is a canonical bijection
   $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc},x}\cong A$
   ([[lem-locally-constant-functions-form-a-sheaf]]);
2. there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of sets
   $$\theta:A_X\longrightarrow\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}$$
   such that for every open $U\subseteq X$ and every $a\in A$ the section
   $\theta_U(\eta_{U}(a))$ is the constant function with value $a$, where
   $\eta:A_{\mathrm{pt}}\to A_X$ is the sheafification map;

   a presheaf of abelian groups ([[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]) and
   $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with pointwise addition is a sheaf of abelian
   groups ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]); the maps
   $a\mapsto\text{the constant function with value }a$ are group homomorphisms,
   and the group structures transported along the bijections $\theta_U$ make
   $A_X$ a sheaf of abelian groups for which every $\eta_U$ and every $\theta_U$
   is a group homomorphism.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.
